heroSub: We start by understanding what you want your money to do. Then we work through five questions that help us organize the decisions, build the plan, put it into motion, and keep it current over time. Where we spend the most time depends on what matters most in your situation.
closingQuote: "This is your one life. Let's design the future income to support it — with confidence, clarity, and intention."

steps.title: Intro Call
steps.p1: A short conversation to see whether your situation matches what we do. We'll walk through the five questions, tell you what we'd need from you, and schedule the next meeting if it makes sense. If it doesn't, we'll say so and point you toward someone better suited. Neither of us gains from proving a bad fit slowly.

steps.title: Discovery
steps.p1: Goals, concerns, and everything the documents don't show. What you want this next season to look like. What you're worried about. Who you're trying to take care of. We'll also gather the statements, tax returns, and policy documents we need in order to give you honest answers instead of general ones.

steps.title: Analysis
steps.p1: This is where the thinking happens. We take what you've told us and what you've built, and run it against the five questions. Tested against bad markets early in retirement, inflation, taxes, and living longer than you planned for. You don't see a spreadsheet. You get answers.

steps.title: Findings
steps.p1: We walk you through what we found. Each of the five questions, answered plainly, along with what would need to change to get where you want to go. We'll go as deep on the reasoning as you want, but we start with the answers, because that's what you came for. At the end, you decide.

groupBIntro: Getting to the plan is the beginning of the relationship. From there, we help put it into motion and continue working with you as life changes.
closingSub: Start with a free 15 to 30 minute Clarity Call. We'll talk about your situation, answer your initial questions, and explain what working with One Life would look like.
clarityP1: Every relationship starts with a free, no-pressure conversation. You tell us what's on your mind. We tell you whether we can help and what working together looks like. If we're not the right fit, we'll say so and point you toward someone who is.
clarityP2: Once we both agree we're a fit, the work begins with Step 1.

after.title: Getting started
after.body:
We help with the setup needed to begin the relationship, including account opening and coordinating transfers with the custodian where appropriate.

We want the transition to be organized and clear so you understand what is happening and what comes next.

after.title: Putting the plan into motion
after.body:
Once we agree on the plan, we help coordinate the steps it calls for.

That may include account transfers, investment changes, beneficiary updates, insurance implementation where appropriate, and coordination with your CPA, attorney, or other professionals when their involvement is needed.

Some steps are handled directly by One Life. Others require the involvement or approval of another professional or financial institution. We help keep the pieces moving together.

after.title: Keeping the plan current
after.body:
This is an ongoing relationship.

Markets change, tax laws change, and your life will change too. We continue reviewing the plan, your investments, and the decisions in front of you as those changes happen.

You can also reach out when something comes up between scheduled reviews. A retirement decision, inheritance, job change, major purchase, family change, or another financial question may be a reason to revisit part of the plan.

The goal is to be in your corner for the long haul, with a plan that continues to reflect your life.

heroTitle: How we build your financial plan.

fiveQ.heading: The five questions.
items: Will your money last as long as you do?
Is your portfolio built for the job it has now?
Are you keeping as much as you should?
Will what's left go where you intend?
fiveQ.note: Still building toward retirement? The first question becomes: will you get where you want to go?

rhythm.heading: What a typical year may look like
rhythm.intro:
Your investment strategy and financial plan are reviewed regularly, with a full review at least annually. Many clients will have additional conversations during the year depending on what is happening and what needs attention.

A typical year might look something like this.

items.title: Spring. Annual review
items.desc: We revisit the five questions, review the investment strategy, and look at what has changed in your financial life since the last full review.

items.title: Summer. Check-in
items.desc: We may revisit cash flow, investments, or another part of the plan that needs attention. Sometimes there is a lot to discuss. Other years there may be very little.

items.title: Fall. Year-end planning
items.desc: We look ahead at tax-related planning opportunities, charitable giving, required distributions, and other decisions that may need to happen before year-end.

items.title: Winter. Starting the new year
items.desc: We can review contribution amounts, beneficiaries, cash needs, and any priorities that have changed for the year ahead.

rhythm.closing: The timing and focus can move depending on your situation. The purpose is to keep the plan current and spend time where it matters most.
